sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Aider is an AI pair programmer that runs in your terminal. You describe a change in plain English, and it edits the files in your git repository, then commits the change with a sensible message so you can review or undo it.
sixtySeconds.problem: Copying code between a chat window and your editor is slow and loses context. Aider works directly on your local codebase, maps the whole project so the model understands it, and keeps every AI change in git.
whoFor: Developers who live in the terminal
People who want AI edits tracked in git
Users who want to pick their own model, cloud or local
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a mature, free, open-source coding assistant that works with almost any LLM and commits every change to git automatically.
requirements: An API key for a model provider, or a local model

overview: Install with the aider-install helper, change into your project folder and start aider with a model and API key. The README shows examples for DeepSeek, Claude Sonnet and OpenAI o3-mini, and Aider can connect to almost any LLM, including local models.

Aider builds a map of your whole codebase so it works well on larger projects, supports dozens of programming languages, and commits each change with a descriptive message. You can also run it in watch mode and ask for changes by writing comments in your IDE.
Extras include adding images and web pages to the chat, voice-to-code, automatic linting and testing after each change, and a copy/paste mode for working through a web chat interface.
